questions.subunit: The Inscribed Angle Theorem (half the central angle)
questions.question: Points A, B, and P lie on circle O. When the central angle ∠AOB for arc AB is 80°, what is the measure of the inscribed angle ∠APB for arc AB, in degrees?
questions.explanation: By the Inscribed Angle Theorem, an inscribed angle is half the central angle subtending the same arc. 80°÷2=40°

questions.subunit: The Inscribed Angle Theorem (half the central angle)
questions.question: Which of the following correctly states the Inscribed Angle Theorem?
choices: The measure of an inscribed angle subtending an arc is half the measure of the central angle subtending that arc
The measure of an inscribed angle subtending an arc is twice the measure of the central angle subtending that arc
The measure of an inscribed angle subtending an arc is equal to the measure of the central angle subtending that arc
The measure of an inscribed angle subtending an arc is one third of the measure of the central angle subtending that arc
questions.answer: The measure of an inscribed angle subtending an arc is half the measure of the central angle subtending that arc
questions.explanation: Inscribed Angle Theorem: an inscribed angle subtending an arc is half the central angle subtending that arc.

questions.subunit: The Inscribed Angle Theorem (half the central angle)
questions.question: In circle O, when the inscribed angle for arc AB is 35°, what is the measure of the central angle ∠AOB for arc AB, in degrees?
questions.explanation: The central angle is twice the inscribed angle. 35°×2=70°

questions.subunit: The Inscribed Angle Theorem (half the central angle)
questions.question: Points A, B, and P lie on circle O. When the central angle ∠AOB for arc AB is 130°, what is the measure of the inscribed angle ∠APB for arc AB, in degrees?
questions.explanation: An inscribed angle is half the central angle. 130°÷2=65°

questions.subunit: Inscribed angles on the same arc
questions.question: Points A, B, P, and Q lie on circle O, with P and Q on the same side of line AB. When the inscribed angle ∠APB for arc AB is 50°, what is the measure of the inscribed angle ∠AQB for the same arc AB, in degrees?
questions.explanation: All inscribed angles subtending the same arc are equal, so ∠AQB=∠APB=50°

questions.subunit: Inscribed angles on the same arc
questions.question: In a single circle, which of the following is true about inscribed angles subtending the same arc?
choices: All inscribed angles subtending the same arc are equal
The measure of an inscribed angle subtending the same arc changes depending on the position of the point on the circle
The sum of two inscribed angles subtending the same arc is 180°
An inscribed angle subtending the same arc is equal to the central angle
questions.answer: All inscribed angles subtending the same arc are equal
questions.explanation: Since every inscribed angle is half the central angle subtending the same arc, all inscribed angles subtending the same arc are equal.

questions.subunit: Inscribed angles on the same arc
questions.question: In a single circle, arc AB and arc CD have equal lengths. When the inscribed angle for arc AB is 28°, what is the measure of the inscribed angle for arc CD, in degrees?
questions.explanation: In a single circle, inscribed angles subtending arcs of equal length are equal. Therefore 28°

questions.subunit: Inscribed angles on the same arc
questions.question: In a single circle, the length of arc AB is twice the length of arc CD. When the inscribed angle for arc CD is 25°, what is the measure of the inscribed angle for arc AB, in degrees?
questions.explanation: In a single circle, the measure of an inscribed angle is proportional to the length of the arc. 25°×2=50°

questions.subunit: The semicircular arc and the right angle
questions.question: Segment AB is a diameter of circle O, and point P is a point on circle O different from A and B. What is the measure of ∠APB, in degrees?
questions.explanation: The central angle for a semicircular arc is 180°, so the inscribed angle is half of that, 90°

questions.subunit: The semicircular arc and the right angle
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the inscribed angle subtending a semicircular arc?
choices: The inscribed angle subtending a semicircular arc is 90°
The inscribed angle subtending a semicircular arc is 180°
The inscribed angle subtending a semicircular arc is 45°
The inscribed angle subtending a semicircular arc is equal to the central angle
questions.answer: The inscribed angle subtending a semicircular arc is 90°
questions.explanation: The central angle subtending a semicircular arc is 180°, and the inscribed angle is half of that, so 90°

questions.subunit: The semicircular arc and the right angle
questions.question: Segment AB is a diameter of circle O, and point P is a point on circle O. When ∠PAB=35°, what is the measure of ∠PBA, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Since AB is a diameter, ∠APB=90°. By the sum of the interior angles of triangle APB, ∠PBA=180°-90°-35°=55°

questions.subunit: The semicircular arc and the right angle
questions.question: Segment AB is a diameter of circle O, and point C is a point on circle O. When ∠CAB=54°, what is the measure of ∠ABC, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Since AB is a diameter, ∠ACB=90°. By the sum of the interior angles of triangle ABC, ∠ABC=180°-90°-54°=36°

questions.subunit: The converse of the Inscribed Angle Theorem
questions.question: Which of the following correctly states the converse of the Inscribed Angle Theorem?
choices: If points P and Q are on the same side of line AB and ∠APB=∠AQB, then the four points A, B, P, and Q lie on a single circle
If points P and Q are on the same side of line AB and ∠APB=∠AQB, then line AB and line PQ are parallel
If points P and Q are on the same side of line AB and ∠APB=∠AQB, then AP=AQ
If the four points A, B, P, and Q lie on a single circle, then the sum of ∠APB and ∠AQB is 180°
questions.answer: If points P and Q are on the same side of line AB and ∠APB=∠AQB, then the four points A, B, P, and Q lie on a single circle
questions.explanation: Converse of the Inscribed Angle Theorem: for two points P and Q on the same side of line AB, if ∠APB=∠AQB, then the four points lie on the same circle.

questions.subunit: The converse of the Inscribed Angle Theorem
questions.question: There are four points A, B, C, and D, with C and D on the same side of line AB. When ∠ACB=40° and ∠ADB=40°, which of the following is true about these four points?
choices: The four points A, B, C, and D lie on a single circle
The four points A, B, C, and D do not lie on a single circle
Whether they lie on a circle depends on the length of segment CD
Whether they lie on a circle depends on the measure of ∠CAB
questions.answer: The four points A, B, C, and D lie on a single circle
questions.explanation: Since C and D are on the same side of line AB and ∠ACB=∠ADB=40°, by the converse of the Inscribed Angle Theorem the four points lie on a single circle.

questions.subunit: The converse of the Inscribed Angle Theorem
questions.question: There are four points A, B, C, and D, with C and D on the same side of line AB. When ∠ACB=50° and ∠ADB=46°, which of the following is true about these four points?
choices: The four points A, B, C, and D do not lie on a single circle
The four points A, B, C, and D lie on a single circle
Since ∠ACB+∠ADB=96°, they lie on a single circle
Whether they lie on a circle cannot be determined
questions.answer: The four points A, B, C, and D do not lie on a single circle
questions.explanation: The points lie on the same circle only when the angles at the two points on the same side are equal. Since 50°≠46°, the four points do not lie on a single circle.

questions.subunit: The converse of the Inscribed Angle Theorem
questions.question: The four points A, B, C, and D lie on a single circle, with C and D on the same side of line AB. When ∠ACB=64°, what is the measure of ∠ADB, in degrees?
questions.explanation: If the four points lie on the same circle, then ∠ACB and ∠ADB are inscribed angles subtending the same arc AB, so they are equal. Therefore 64°

questions.subunit: Cyclic quadrilaterals (advanced)
questions.question: Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle. When ∠A=95°, what is the measure of ∠C, in degrees?
questions.explanation: In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite angles is 180°. ∠C=180°-95°=85°

questions.subunit: Cyclic quadrilaterals (advanced)
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct property of a cyclic quadrilateral?
choices: The sum of opposite angles is 180°
The sum of opposite angles is 90°
Opposite angles are equal
The sum of adjacent angles is 180°
questions.answer: The sum of opposite angles is 180°
questions.explanation: In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite angles is 180°.

questions.subunit: Cyclic quadrilaterals (advanced)
questions.question: Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle, and ∠BAD=105°. When point E is taken on the line extending side BC in the direction of C, what is the measure of ∠DCE, in degrees?
questions.explanation: By the sum of opposite angles, ∠BCD=180°-105°=75°. Since ∠DCE is adjacent to ∠BCD, it is 180°-75°=105°. An exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the interior angle opposite the adjacent interior angle.

questions.subunit: Cyclic quadrilaterals (advanced)
questions.question: Quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle, and the measure of ∠A is twice the measure of ∠C. What is the measure of ∠A, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Since ∠A+∠C=180° and ∠A=2∠C, we get 3∠C=180°, so ∠C=60°. Therefore ∠A=120°

questions.subunit: Tangents to a circle and angles
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct property of a tangent to a circle?
choices: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency
A tangent to a circle is parallel to the radius drawn to the point of tangency
A tangent to a circle always passes through the center of the circle
A tangent to a circle intersects the circle at two points
questions.answer: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency
questions.explanation: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency. This is the fundamental property of a tangent.

questions.subunit: Tangents to a circle and angles
questions.question: From point P outside circle O, two tangents are drawn to circle O, with points of tangency A and B. Since the two tangent segments drawn from a single external point are equal in length, PA=PB. When ∠APB=40°, what is the measure of ∠PAB, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Since PA=PB, triangle PAB is isosceles. ∠PAB=(180°-40°)÷2=70°

questions.subunit: Tangents to a circle and angles
questions.question: From point P outside circle O, two tangents are drawn to circle O, with points of tangency A and B. When ∠APB=50°, what is the measure of the central angle ∠AOB, in degrees?
questions.explanation: Since a tangent is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency, ∠OAP=∠OBP=90°. Because the sum of the interior angles of quadrilateral OAPB is 360°, ∠AOB=360°-90°-90°-50°=130°

questions.subunit: Tangents to a circle and angles
questions.question: Let AT be the line tangent to circle O at point A on the circle, and draw chord AB. When the angle between the tangent and the chord, ∠TAB=65°, what is the measure of the inscribed angle subtending arc AB that lies inside ∠TAB, in degrees?
questions.explanation: By the Tangent-Chord Angle theorem (inscribed angle in the alternate segment), the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the inscribed angle subtending the arc that lies inside that angle. Therefore 65°
